Robert Ellington Jr.''' (born November 29, 1987) is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is a player development coach for the [[Miami Heat]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Known for his shooting ability, he was nicknamed "'''the Man With The Golden Arm'''".{{Cite web |title=Status upgrade: Wayne Ellington's 'golden arm' goes platinum as Pistons shooting star heats up |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/features/status-upgrade-wayne-ellingtons-golden-arm-goes-platinum-pistons-shooting-star-heats |access-date=2023-10-15 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} He played for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|University of North Carolina]] from 2006 to 2009. He chose to forgo his final season of college eligibility to declare for the [[2009 NBA draft]], and was drafted 28th overall by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. ==High school career== Ellington scored 2,211 points in his high school career, tallying 455 points at [[Daniel Boone Area High School|Daniel Boone High School]], and then 1,756 points at [[The Episcopal Academy]].{{Cite web |url=http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/ellington_wayne00.html |title=Wayne Ellington |access-date=February 20, 2007 |archive-date=February 21, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070221070759/http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/ellington_wayne00.html |url-status=dead }} In his senior year, Ellington averaged 21.9 points, 8.3 rebounds, 3.2 assists and shot 39% from the three-point line. He led Episcopal to an overall record of 52–7 in his junior and senior year, and to the [[Inter-Academic League]] Conference title in his last two years going 20–0 in both seasons. (Episcopal doesn't play in state championships.) Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Ellington was listed as the No. 1 shooting guard and the No. 8 player in the nation in 2006.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Wayne-Ellington-25394;_ylt=AoyurCLJRlZozUxtyE0AYJZGPZB4 Wayne Ellington Recruiting Profile] ==College career== [[File:Wayne Ellington cropped.jpg|thumb|left|180 px|Ellington with the North Carolina Tar Heels in 2009]] Ellington played in all 38 games for the ACC Champion Tar Heels in 2006–07, averaging 11.7 points per game. He was named to the 2007 ACC All-Tournament Team. His season ended on a sour note though, as North Carolina lost to Georgetown in the East Regional final of the NCAA Tournament. He had a chance to win the game in regulation, but missed a 3-pointer in the final seconds. Ellington was a member of the U.S. national team that finished fifth at the [[2007 Pan American Games]]. As a sophomore, Ellington saw his points-per-game average increase as the Tar Heels increasingly went to him in key moments of games. In the January 6, 2008, game at Clemson, Ellington scored a career high 36 points, including the game winning three-pointer with 0:00.4 seconds left in overtime to lead top-rated UNC over #19 Clemson 90–88."[https://web.archive.org/web/20080110123230/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280060228 UNC escapes OT at Clemson thanks to last-second 3-pointer by Ellington]." ''ESPN.com.'' Retrieved on January 7, 2008 But again, his season ended in a poor fashion, as he shot only 1 for 9 from three-point range, in a loss to Kansas in a national semifinal game in the NCAA Tournament. He declared for the [[2008 NBA draft]] after that season, but did not hire an [[sports agent|agent]], and withdrew to play his junior year at North Carolina.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2009/news/story?id=4091170 |title=Lawson, Ellington entering draft |agency=Associated Press |work=ESPN.com |date=April 23, 2009 |access-date=April 24, 2009}} As a Junior, Ellington helped lead the [[2008–09 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|Tar Heels]] to the [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|National Championship]], where they defeated the Michigan State Spartans 89–72. He shot 7–10 from three-point range in the Final Four, and he was named to the All-Tournament Team and was named [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player]]. During his college career, Ellington averaged 14.7 points, 4.1 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/e/ellinwa01.html#all_all_college_stats|title=Wayne Ellington Stats {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=December 3, 2018}} On April 23, 2009, Ellington announced that he would forgo his senior season and enter the [[NBA draft]]. ==Professional career== ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2009–2012)=== [[File:Wayne Ellington.jpg|thumb|289x289px|Ellington as a member of the Minnesota Timberwolves]] Ellington was drafted 28th overall by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]].Taylor, Nate. [http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/49150517.html Last first-round pick delivers guard only sweep] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090705144744/http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/49150517.html |date=July 5, 2009 }}, ''[[Minneapolis Star-Tribune]]'', June 26, 2009. He averaged 6.6 points per game and 2.1 rebounds per game in his rookie season off of the bench. ===Memphis Grizzlies (2012–2013)=== On July 24, 2012, Ellington was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for forward [[Dante Cunningham]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_acquire_wayne_ellington-120729 | title=Grizzlies acquire Wayne Ellington |work=NBA.com| date=July 24, 2012| access-date=July 25, 2012}} On November 11, 2012, Ellington scored a career-high 25 points on 7-of-11 three-pointers in a 104–96 win over the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20121111/MIAMEM/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Grizzlies 104, Heat 86|work=NBA.com|date=November 11, 2012|access-date=January 14, 2017}} On January 7, 2013, he set a new career high with 26 points in a 113–81 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130107/MEMSAC/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Grizzlies 113, Kings [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite news|title=Lakers Sign Wayne Ellington|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/140922_wayneEllington|access-date=September 22, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=September 22, 2014}} On November 11, 2014, he took an indefinite leave of absence from the Lakers after his father was shot and killed in Philadelphia.[http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/lakersnow/la-sp-ln-lakers-wayne-ellington-father-shot-and-killed-20141111-story.html Lakers' Wayne Ellington takes leave after fatal shooting of his father] He returned to action on November 21, 2014. On January 27, 2015, he scored a career-high 28 points in a 98–92 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20150127/WASLAL/gameinfo.html Wall's Wizards rally, send Lakers to 9th straight loss 98-92] He finished the season having played 65 games after being ruled out for the rest of the season on April 2, 2015, with a shoulder injury.[http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/150402_ellington_injury_update Wayne Ellington Injury Update] ===Brooklyn Nets (2015–2016)=== On July 10, 2015, Ellington signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/brooklyn-nets-sign-wayne-ellington|title=BROOKLYN NETS SIGN WAYNE ELLINGTON|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 10, 2015|access-date=July 10, 2015}} On December 28, 2015, he scored a season-high 26 points and tied a career high with seven made three-pointers in a 111–105 win over the Miami Heat.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151228/BKNMIA/gameinfo.html|title=Ellington's 7 3-pointers help Nets rally past Heat, 111-105|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=December 28, 2015|access-date=December 28, 2015}} On April 27, 2016, Ellington was named recipient of the 2015–16 [[J. Walter Kennedy Citizenship Award]] as selected by the [[Pro Basketball Writers Association]] (PBWA).[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2016/04/27/ellington-win-2015-16-j-walter-kennedy-citizenship-award Nets' Wayne Ellington Wins 2015-16 J. Walter Kennedy Citizenship Award] ===Miami Heat (2016–2019)=== On July 10, 2016, Ellington signed with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-announce-free-agent-signings|title=HEAT Announce Free Agent Signings|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 10, 2016|access-date=July 10, 2016}} He made his debut for the Heat on November 28, 2016, against the [[Boston Celtics]] after missing the first 16 games of the season with a bruised thigh; he played 27 minutes and scored nine points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899706|title=Thomas scores 25, Celtics get past Heat 112-104|work=ESPN.com|date=November 28, 2016|access-date=November 29, 2016}} On December 22, 2017, Ellington tied a career high with 28 points and had a career-high eight 3-pointers in a 113–101 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975225|title=Ellington ties career-best with 28, Heat top Mavs 113-101|work=ESPN.com|date=December 22, 2017|access-date=December 23, 2017}} On March 21, 2018, in a 119–98 win over the [[New York Knicks]], Ellington hit his 200th 3-pointer of the season, making him the third Heat player with that many in a season, joining [[Damon Jones]] (225) and [[Tim Hardaway|Tim Hardaway Sr.]] (203).{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975814|title=Olynyk's big night helps Heat past Knicks, 119-98|work=ESPN.com|date=March 21, 2018|access-date=March 22, 2018}} In the Heat's regular season finale on April 11, 2018, Ellington scored a career-high 32 points while setting Miami's single-season record for 3-pointers, as the Heat wrapped up the No. 6 seed in the Eastern Conference playoffs by beating the [[Toronto Raptors]] 116–109 in overtime. Ellington needed six 3-pointers in the finale to beat the record of 225 that Jones set in the 2004–05 season. He finished the season with 227.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975967|title=Ellington sets Heat record, Miami tops Toronto 116-109|work=ESPN.com|date=April 11, 2018|access-date=April 11, 2018}} On July 13, 2018, Ellington re-signed with the Heat.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-re-signs-wayne-ellington|title=HEAT Re-Signs Wayne Ellington|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2018|access-date=July 13, 2018}} On February 6, 2019, Ellington was traded, along with [[Tyler Johnson (basketball)|Tyler Johnson]], to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for [[Ryan Anderson (basketball, born 1988)|Ryan Anderson]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-acquire-tyler-johnson-wayne-ellington-miami|title=Suns Acquire Tyler Johnson, Wayne Ellington from Miami|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2019|access-date=February 6, 2019}} He was waived by the Suns the following day.{{cite
